title: Narrowing unknown at API and JSON boundaries
hook: fetch and JSON.parse return unknown at the trust boundary — TypeScript will not let you read .email until you narrow. Senior interviews and Reddit threads treat unknown-at-boundaries as the fix for any: validate shape, then the compiler trusts you inside the block.

blocks.text: **unknown** is the type-safe top type: you can assign anything to it, but you cannot use it until you **narrow** with typeof, instanceof, in checks, or a user-defined type guard. At **API boundaries** — `response.json()`, Redis payloads, WebSocket messages, `process.env` — data is untrusted. TypeScript does not parse JSON into your interface at runtime; **erasable types** vanish on emit. The pattern: parse to `unknown`, run a **validator** (manual checks, Zod, Valibot), then work with a typed value.

entries.plainDefinition: Top type that forces narrowing before use — safer than any.
Function returning x is T that tells the compiler narrowing succeeded.
entries.example: function isUser(x: unknown): x is User { ... }

entries.plainDefinition: Line where external data enters your program — assume hostile until validated.
entries.example: HTTP response body, message queue payload.

entries.plainDefinition: Function that throws if narrow fails — asserts parameter type for rest of block.
entries.example: function assertUser(x: unknown): asserts x is User

blocks.text: `as User` after json() is a lie — production APIs change fields, return null, or nest errors. `any` silences the compiler and ships runtime `undefined is not a function`. C# deserializes with System.Text.Json into typed models but still throws on mismatch — TypeScript has no runtime unless you add validation. Redis `GET` returns string | null — parse then narrow. FAANG code review rejects `as` casts at boundaries without guards.

blocks.title: Interview trap: any vs unknown
blocks.body: any disables checking — unknown forces you to prove shape. Prefer unknown on every external input; reserve any for migration only.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Validate structure
items.body: Type guard or schema library checks required fields and types.

items.title: Branch on failure
items.body: Return 502, log, or throw — never proceed with partial trust.

items.title: Use narrowed type
items.body: Inside if (isUser(raw)) block, raw is User — full IntelliSense.

diagram.title: unknown narrowing at boundary
diagram.source:
flowchart TD
  EXT[External JSON] --> U[unknown]
  U --> G{Type guard / schema}
  G -->|pass| T[Typed domain model]
  G -->|fail| E[Error response]
  T --> APP[Application logic]

snippet.label: Manual type guard for API User
snippet.explanation: Line 9: null check — typeof null is 'object' in JS. Line 16: raw unknown until line 17 guard. Line 18: return raw as User — compiler knows shape.

snippet.label: Redis cache boundary — parse then narrow
snippet.explanation: Line 19: JSON.parse returns any by default — assign to unknown first. Line 21: corrupt cache deleted — fail safe. Line 24: narrowed Session.

snippet.label: asserts function — throw to narrow
snippet.explanation: Line 1: asserts keyword — no return value, control flow narrows. Line 8: after assertIsUser, body typed as User in rest of function.

snippet.label: Failure mode — unsafe cast after json()
snippet.explanation: Line 1: as User bypasses validation — most common production TS bug at boundaries. Fix: unknown + guard.

blocks.title: Trusting OpenAPI types without runtime check
blocks.body: Generated interfaces describe intent — server can still return wrong JSON. Validate at boundary or use contract tests.

blocks.title: Shallow guards
blocks.body: Checking only typeof value === 'object' is not enough — validate every field you read.

blocks.text: Senior answers mention schema libraries (Zod infer types from schema — single source of truth), discriminated unions for API error envelopes `{ ok: true, data } | { ok: false, error }`, and narrowing in catch with unknown (TypeScript 4.4+). Production: log validation failures with request id, never leak raw payload to client. Compare to C# nullable reference types — compile-time only like strictNullChecks; both need runtime validation at boundaries.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Using any for json(). Saying TypeScript validates JSON at runtime. Cannot write isUser guard. Not knowing unknown vs any difference. Skipping null check in object guard.

interviewTakeaways: unknown at every external input — narrow before property access.
Type guards (x is T) and asserts functions for control-flow narrowing.
JSON.parse and fetch.json() do not produce your interface — validate.
60s: unknown forces proof. Manual guard or Zod. Redis and fetch are trust boundaries. any silences compiler. C# JsonSerializer throws but TS types erase.
Follow-up: discriminated union for API success/error envelope.
commonPitfalls: Weak: as User after json() — runtime mismatch.
Weak: any at boundary — defeats TypeScript.
Strong: 'unknown in, guard validates shape, narrowed type in block. Corrupt Redis key deleted. Zod for DRY schema+type.'

jsTsCorrelations.note: JavaScript has no unknown — same validation logic runs at runtime; TypeScript adds compile-time narrowing after guards.
unknown is the type-safe replacement for any at boundaries — assignable from anything, usable only after narrow.
